sentences.text: The genus name Aepyornithomimus translates to 'Aepyornis mimic', highlighting its resemblance to the large ratite Aepyornis in foot structure.
Paleontologists Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig and Philip J. Currie formally described this animal in 2017.
Finding this diagnostic ornithomimosaur in early, dry deposits suggests the group could tolerate various environmental conditions.
Scientists propose that Aepyornithomimus displays an intermediate metatarsal condition between basal and more derived ornithomimosaurs.
Aepyornithomimus is a member of the infraorder Ornithomimosauria.
It is further classified within the family Ornithomimidae.
This creature inhabited Asia during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 83 to 70 million years ago.
Its fossils come from the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia.
The Djadochta Formation represents an arid eolian desert environment comparable to today's Gobi Desert.
